question: Should experimental grouped-Claw update planning, including its capability-consent and integrity-token contract, be accepted as a core OpenClaw lifecycle surface before the dependent executor lands?
rationale: This is a new core product and security-boundary contract, not a repair to an established behavior; code review alone cannot select the permanent owner boundary or consent model.

options.title: Sponsor the staged core design
options.body: Approve the read-only planner as the core primitive, contingent on final-head redacted behavior proof and normal stack-order review.

options.title: Keep lifecycle work outside core
options.body: Direct the proposal toward an external plugin or ClawHub-owned workflow if the core should not own grouped package reconciliation and consent semantics.

options.title: Narrow the contract first
options.body: Request a smaller diagnostics-only or schema-only primitive before accepting the update planning and consent surface.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the staged core design
recommendation.body: Approve the read-only planner as the core primitive, contingent on final-head redacted behavior proof and normal stack-order review.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick-Erichsen is assigned and supplied the most concrete lifecycle-planning review requirements in the PR discussion.
